primary_sources: Treaty of Fort Laramie (Horse Creek Treaty), September 17, 1851

stimulus.source_note: Treaty of Fort Laramie (Horse Creek Treaty), September 17, 1851, Articles 1, 2, 3, and 7, as signed. Public domain. Note: the Senate ratified the treaty with an amendment changing the Article 7 annuity from fifty years to ten years (plus up to five discretionary years), May 24, 1852.
stimulus.text: The aforesaid nations... do hereby covenant and agree to abstain in future from all hostilities whatever against each other... The aforesaid nations do hereby recognize the right of the United States Government to establish roads, military and other posts, within their respective territories... In consideration of the rights and privileges acknowledged in the preceding article, the United States bind themselves to protect the aforesaid Indian nations against the commission of all depredations by the people of the said United States... the United States bind themselves to deliver to the said Indian nations the sum of Fifty thousand dollars per annum for fifty years in provisions, merchandize, domestic animals and agricultural implement.

source: original; stimulus is a verbatim excerpt from the Treaty of Fort Laramie, September 17, 1851, public domain
stem: The treaty is best understood in the context of which of the following developments?

options.text: The end of the Civil War and the start of Reconstruction.
options.misconception: The treaty was signed in 1851, a decade before the Civil War began.

options.text: The purchase of Alaska from Russia.
options.misconception: Alaska was purchased in 1867, sixteen years after the treaty.

options.text: The large migration across the Great Plains in the 1840s and 1850s.
The construction of the transcontinental railroad.
options.misconception: The railroad was built in the 1860s; the treaty came in 1851, before it.

rationales.A: The treaty was signed in September 1851, ten years before the Civil War began.
rationales.B: Alaska was bought in 1867, sixteen years after this treaty.
rationales.C: Hundreds of thousands of migrants were crossing the Plains on the overland trails, and the treaty arranged peace, roads, and posts along their route. Background: the council gathered about 10,000 Plains Indians near Fort Laramie.
rationales.D: The transcontinental railroad was built in the 1860s; this treaty predates it by a decade.
rationales.general:
1. Date the treaty. It was signed in September 1851.
2. Ask what was happening on the Plains then. About 300,000 migrants were traveling the overland trails west.
3. Match the treaty to that movement. It promised peace, roads, and posts — the things a migration route needs.
Remember: treaties often follow traffic. When thousands of wagons cross someone's land, a treaty is how the government tries to manage the meeting.
